summary: The narrator and Alan, with pilot Lieutenant Villatoro, are flying a helicopter low through rain over dense jungle, following a river toward a possible location. The narrator spots a clearing and they land on a paved plaza, where a brand-new-looking stepped Mayan-style pyramid looms nearby. Alan dismisses it as 'Jungle Disneyland' and notes plenty of Army presence in the area, and the passage ends with the pilot staring at the pyramid.
one_line: A helicopter crew descends through storm-lashed jungle and lands on a plaza beneath a new-looking Mayan pyramid.
key_facts: The narrator and Alan are flying along a river through heavy rain, hoping to find a location they believe is nearby.
The narrator spots an opening in the trees and asks Alan whether they can set down there and let the storm blow over.
Alan orders Lieutenant Villatoro to bank and go back for a look, and they confirm an opening in the trees.
The narrator notices a hill topped by a stone building that is clearly man-made.
The pyramid appears brand new to the narrator.
Alan describes the place as 'Jungle Disneyland' and says the deal is not about Mickey Mouse.
Alan says there is plenty of Army hanging out around the area.
Lieutenant Villatoro guides the chopper's descent until it is only a few feet above the ground.
The rotor causes surface effect, throwing a spray off the paving stones that glisten under the landing lights.
The pyramid stands over one side of a large plaza that is mostly hidden from the sky by swaying trees.
The stepped pyramid is described as being in the classic Mayan style.
The Bell helicopter's skids thump onto the stones as it lands.
Villatoro is described as an ex-Army pilot who keeps glancing at the pyramid.
